paper.title: Virtual Node Graph Neural Network for Full Phonon Prediction
paper.research_summary: The paper introduces the Virtual Node Graph Neural Network (VGNN) to predict phonon spectra and bandstructures directly from atomic coordinates, addressing challenges of variable-length output and complex unit cells. It presents three variants—vector virtual nodes (VVN), matrix virtual nodes (MVN), and momentum-dependent matrix virtual nodes (k-MVN)—to predict Γ-point phonons and full dispersion. The method is validated on alloy systems and used to build a Γ-phonon database of over 146,000 materials from the Materials Project.

tasks.objective: Direct prediction of Γ-phonon spectra and full phonon bandstructures from atomic coordinates
constraints: input limited to atomic coordinates only
no prior knowledge of interatomic forces
must handle variable/complex unit cells (up to 400+ atoms per unit cell)
output_goal: 3m Γ-phonon energies for m-atom unit cell
full phonon band structure at arbitrary k-points in Brillouin zone

evidence.text: By developing three types of virtual node approaches - the vector, matrix, and momentum-dependent matrix virtual nodes, we achieve direct prediction of Γ-phonon spectra and full dispersion only using atomic coordinates as input.
We study materials’ phonon spectra and dispersion relations, given that phonons bands are challenging to compute or measure with high computational cost and limited experimental resources.
Our work offers an efﬁcient technique that can compute zone-center phonon energies and full phonon band structures directly from atomic structures in complex materials

evidence.text: The data set contains material structures (the same as the primitive structure obtained from the Material Project12), second-order derivatives of energies with respect to atomic perturbations for regular points inside the irreducible zone, and phonon dispersion along highly symmetric paths of 1,521 crystalline inorganic materials.
All models randomly split the data into 90% training (1,365 materials), and 10% testing (156 materials) sets.
We used them as our complex material data set.

stages.stage_name_raw: training of VGNN models (VVN, MVN, k-MVN)
stages.stage_goal: Optimize neural network parameters to minimize MSE loss between predicted and ground-truth phonon frequencies

evidence.text: The model is optimized by minimizing the mean squared error (MSE) loss function between the phonon of the training data set and the one predicted by the model after normalizing them by the maximum phonon frequency of each material.
We optimize the values of the training parameters. The set of parameters that gives the best results for VVN, MVN, k-MVN are shown in Table S1.
evidence.section: III NEURAL NETWORK TRAINING AND OPTIMIZATION

stages.stage_goal: Assess model performance on test sets using loss distribution and correlation plots

evidence.text: Evaluation of the test accuracy through the distribution of loss function and correlation plot between ground-truth and predicted average phonon frequencies, respectively.

stages.stage_name_raw: validation on alloy systems and complex materials
stages.stage_goal: Validate model generalizability on unseen alloy systems and large-unit-cell materials
stage_output: demonstration of scalability to >40 atoms/unit cell

evidence.text: Additional tests on SiGe alloys, FeCoNi alloys, and other high-energy alloys are performed, which agree well with existing literature (Supplementary Information VI).
We demonstrate the power of this approach with the binary alloy of SiGe.
evidence.section: VI.2 Phonon Prediction in Alloy Systems

evidence.text: We have shown that our k-MVN model could handle phonon prediction of binary and ternary alloys. Here we demonstrate even higher component alloys.
evidence.section: VI.2 Phonon Prediction in Alloy Systems

here we present a new phonon database containing the phonon spectra for the entire 146,323 Materials in Materials Project (MP) as of 2022 computed by the MVN approach.
